summary:
Bilecik province stands under the national framework applicable across Turkey, and the sources carried for this record contain no Bilecik-specific law, enforcement practice or local ordinance. Whatever local variation exists is undocumented here, so the national picture is what a visitor to Bilecik should expect to encounter.

The most consequential pending measure is the leaked '11th Judicial Package', a draft omnibus justice package reported by Human Rights Watch on 29 October 2025. If adopted as drafted it would amend the penal and civil codes to criminalise behaviour deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality', and would punish participation in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony with up to four years in prison. The draft carried in the inventory makes no provision specific to Bilecik, so its reach would be uniform.

The same draft would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming health care, including surgery, from 18 to 25 and would require permanent infertility as a condition, while punishing the health professionals who perform such care. Human Rights Watch describes the package as one of the most alarming rollbacks of LGBT rights in decades. Fifteen Turkish LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association oppose the draft.

Hostility toward LGBT people in Turkey has been institutionalised as explicit state policy rather than left to residual prejudice, according to the Kaos GL report 'A major siege against LGBTI+ people in 2025: Hostility turned into state policy'. The report documents senior officials' hate speech and instructions issued to public institutions under a 'Year of the Family' banner, creating a climate that encouraged human-rights violations, alongside systematic restriction of freedom of expression and artistic freedom by regulatory and supervisory bodies. Findings were presented by lawyer Kerem Dikmen at the launch.
tangentialFactors:
The draft package sits alongside enforcement already running ahead of legislation. The national framework recorded in the parent profile shows police conducting identity checks on trans women in Istanbul through 2025 and detaining them for record-keeping even though the measure had not been passed, which indicates that a pending statute in Turkey does not guarantee a pause in street-level action against trans people.

The care provisions in the draft would tighten a regime that is already narrowing. A Health Ministry regulation reported in September 2025 barred hospitals from recording the 'other' option on medical-board reports and required e-reports to be issued, changes that risk profiling trans patients in official records. An age floor of 25 with a permanent infertility condition would sit on top of that reporting machinery.

Restriction of expression by regulatory and supervisory bodies, as documented by Kaos GL for 2025, is adjacent to the risks a visitor faces at checkpoints and in public space: the same institutional direction that curbs artistic and expressive freedom also underpins the discriminatory rhetoric recorded around Pride events.
localsOnly:
For residents of Bilecik the draft '11th Judicial Package' would operate directly on the civil and penal codes they live under, criminalising conduct defined against 'biological sex and general morality' and attaching prison terms of up to four years to participation in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony.

Transition-related care would be affected at both ends. The minimum age for gender-affirming health care would move from 18 to 25 with permanent infertility required, and health professionals performing such care would face punishment, which places the burden of the change on patients and clinicians in Bilecik's health facilities alike.

Kaos GL's 2025 findings describe instructions issued to public institutions under a 'Year of the Family' banner and systematic restriction of freedom of expression and artistic freedom by regulatory and supervisory bodies, conditions that shape the environment for residents organising, performing or publishing locally.

Opposition to the draft has come from fifteen Turkish LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association, and the report's findings were presented by lawyer Kerem Dikmen at the launch event.
outOfScopeNotes:
No source in the inventory addresses Bilecik directly. There is no record of local police practice, municipal ordinances, Pride or visibility events, detention figures, or the availability of transition-related care in the province, so the local picture is unresolved rather than documented as benign.

The '11th Judicial Package' is carried as a leaked draft reported on 29 October 2025. Whether it has since been introduced, amended or adopted is not sourced here, and the record does not establish its current legislative status.

The inventory does not state whether the age-25 care threshold or the penalties for health professionals have any transitional arrangement, regional exemption or enforcement guidance, and no Bilecik health facility is identified as either providing or refusing transition-related care.

Whether the expression restrictions documented by Kaos GL have been applied through any body operating in Bilecik is not sourced; the report's findings are national in scope and are not broken down by province in the material carried here.
